C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit girls in rest stops, bars and restaurants along the Maputo–South Africa highway and around mines, and that non-state armed groups abducted children and sexually exploited girls. Girls as young as 11 working as nannies are vulnerable when employment ends.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Mozambique

C.n: Zimbabwe — sex trafficking around gold and diamond mines; girls traded under ngozi (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers at mining sites; families
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit women and children in sex trafficking around mines, sometimes for money or food, and may exploit children as panners and ore couriers in gold and diamond mines. Traditional practices including trading daughters for food or money and ngozi — giving a relative to another family to atone for a killing — make girls vulnerable. Low-level official complicity persisted.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Zimbabwe

C.n: DR Congo — forced labour and sexual exploitation of children at eastern artisanal mines (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Mining bosses, miners, family members, government officials, armed groups
C.cover: Traffickers named in the report include government officials; corruption and complicity contributed to impunity.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says mining bosses, other miners, family members, government officials and armed groups force or coerce adults and children into forced labour in artisanal mines in eastern DRC, including through debt bondage, and that most trafficking is internal, including sex trafficking and forced marriage of girls.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Democratic Republic of the Congo

C.n: Côte d'Ivoire — girls brought to Abidjan for domestic servitude; Nigerian girls at mines (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Relatives and Nigerian trafficking networks
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says distant relatives bring girls from rural Côte d'Ivoire and other West African countries to Abidjan for school or training and then exploit them in domestic servitude, where they are vulnerable to sexual exploitation; Ivorian women and girls are sex-trafficked especially in Abidjan; and Nigerian traffickers recruit women and girls for shop jobs then exploit them in gold-mining and cocoa regions.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Côte d'Ivoire

C.n: South Africa — rural children trafficked to Gauteng and Western Cape (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Brothel owners and traffickers; some parents
C.cover: Low-level official corruption and complicity persisted.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers recruit victims from rural areas, especially children, and exploit them in sex trafficking in cities, especially Gauteng and Western Cape; brothel owners use drugs to control victims including children; and some parents exploit their children in sex trafficking or online sexual exploitation for money or drugs.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — South Africa

C.n: Ethiopia — girls trafficked to Djibouti, Sudan and Saudi Arabia (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers and begging rings
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Ethiopian women and children in forced begging, sometimes via organized begging rings, in Saudi Arabia, and exploit Ethiopian girls in domestic servitude and sex trafficking in neighbouring countries, particularly Djibouti and Sudan, sometimes using drugs for control. Reports of official complicity continued.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Ethiopia

C.n: Nepal → India — trafficking of girls to Indian brothels (estimates)
C.vn: Published annual estimates range from 5,000–10,000 women and girls (Koirala et al.; Poudel & Carryer 2000) and 7,000–10,000 girls aged 9–16 (Aengst 2001); UNDP 2004 said about 20% of those trafficked are under 16
C.who: Trafficking networks recruiting via false job, marriage and online romance offers
C.cover: US TIP 2025: serious concerns of official complicity; traffickers bribe some Indian officials to fly Nepali workers to third countries.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers use job offers and online romance scams to recruit Nepali women and children to India for sex trafficking; Nepali courts convicted 406 traffickers (231 for sex trafficking) in the year. A 2024 study it cites found a majority of workers in Nepal's adult entertainment sector were sex-trafficking victims, nearly half of them children. Research collated on Wikipedia gives estimates of 5,000–10,000 Nepali women and girls trafficked to India each year across a 1,850 km open border.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Nepal; Wikipedia 'Human trafficking in Nepal' (citing Koirala et al., Aengst 2001, UNDP 2004, ILO 2001)

C.n: Kolkata red-light areas — rescues of trafficked Nepali girls and minors (2015, 2025)
C.vn: six Nepali girls (Jan 2015, IJM-assisted raid) plus nine minor girls rescued in Burtolla (Sept 2025)
C.who: Brothel keepers and traffickers in Kolkata
C.d: In January 2015 police, with International Justice Mission and three NGOs, freed six young women trafficked from Nepal from four brothels in Kolkata's largest red-light area; all had fake adult ID documents, which IJM said traffickers issue to underage girls. On 10 September 2025 Kolkata Police's Anti-Human Trafficking Unit rescued ten people including nine minor girls from a house in Burtolla, North Kolkata, and arrested six people, including the couple running it (charged). The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers recruit significant numbers of Nepali and Bangladeshi women and girls for sex trafficking in India.
C.cite: IJM Canada, 22 Jan 2015; IANS via Free Press Journal, 11 Sep 2025; US TIP 2025 — India

C.n: Kamathipura, Mumbai — red-light district fed by trafficking from Nepal and Indian states
C.who: Brothels of Kamathipura
C.d: Kamathipura, Mumbai's oldest and largest red-light district and one of Asia's largest, was established over 150 years ago under British rule; the BBC in 2013 put its sex workers at an estimated 20,000. Girls were trafficked there from poor villages in other Indian states, some as young as 11, on promises of domestic work. The 2025 US Trafficking in Persons report is cited, though it could not be opened for this map, for a shift of sex trafficking in India toward spas, hotels and private residences, and for 2022 crime-data figures of 204 convicted traffickers and 1,134 acquittals; that report could not be opened in this pass (state.gov blocked).
C.cite: BBC News, 'Mumbai red light district: trafficked girls' (interview with photojournalist Hazel Thompson), 23 Nov 2013

C.n: Bangladesh — girls trafficked to India, Pakistan and the Gulf; Rohingya girls near Cox's Bazar (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers, recruitment agents, armed groups in Rohingya camps
C.cover: Corruption and official complicity were significant concerns; corrupt policing in Rohingya camps.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Bangladeshi women and girls in sex trafficking abroad, including in India, Pakistan and Gulf countries, and observers estimate children are 40 per cent of Bangladeshi sex-trafficking victims exploited abroad. Tourists have increased demand for sexual exploitation, including of Rohingya girls, near Cox's Bazar, where more than one million Rohingya refugees live in 33 camps. Courts convicted 103 traffickers, down from 407.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Bangladesh

C.n: Pakistan → China — 629 girls and women sold as 'brides' (AP 2019)
C.vn: girls and women on a list compiled by Pakistani investigators, from 2018 to June 2019
C.who: Brokers selling poor (often Christian) Pakistani girls and women to Chinese men
C.cover: Officials told AP the investigation largely stopped after June 2019 because of pressure from government officials fearful of harming ties with Beijing; in October 2019 a Faisalabad court acquitted 31 Chinese nationals after witnesses were threatened or bribed into silence.
C.d: AP obtained a list compiled by Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency of 629 girls and women sold as brides to Chinese men from 2018 to mid-2019. In October 2019 a court in Faisalabad acquitted 31 Chinese nationals charged in the biggest case. The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers target impoverished Christian communities to send women and girls to China, where hundreds reported being forced into commercial sex.
C.cite: Associated Press via Al Jazeera, 5 Dec 2019; US TIP 2025 — Pakistan

C.n: Myanmar → China — Kachin women and girls sold as 'brides' (HRW 2019)
C.vn: Myanmar government reported 226 cases in 2017; HRW interviewed 37 survivors and said the true number is likely much higher
C.who: Traffickers including relatives and acquaintances; buying families in China
C.cover: HRW said Myanmar and Chinese authorities were 'looking away'; police on both sides gave traffickers little reason to fear enforcement.
C.d: Human Rights Watch's 112-page report of 21 March 2019 documented women and girls from Kachin and northern Shan States, many displaced by conflict, sold for US$3,000–13,000 to Chinese families, locked up and raped so they would become pregnant. One survivor was trafficked at 16 by her sister-in-law. The 2025 US TIP report says displaced women and girls in Kachin and Shan remain vulnerable to forced marriage and forced childbearing in China.
C.cite: Human Rights Watch, 'Give Us a Baby and We'll Let You Go', 21 Mar 2019; US TIP 2025 — Burma

C.n: Vietnam and Laos → China — girls sold as brides (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers and marriage brokers
C.d: The 2025 US TIP reports say traffickers in Vietnamese border villages lure women and girls, particularly Hmong, to China for forced marriages involving sex trafficking or forced labour, and use 'bride kidnapping' to exploit ethnic-minority girls in the northwest highlands; in Laos, traffickers increasingly kidnap or recruit women and girls via marriage brokers to China for sex trafficking, forced labour and forced surrogacy. Vietnam identified 236 child victims in 2024.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Vietnam; Laos

C.n: Swiss bar owner jailed 16 years for abusing more than 80 boys in Pattaya and northern Thailand
C.vn: more than 80 boys, some as young as nine or ten
C.who: Unnamed Swiss national (72, from Lucerne) who ran a bar in Pattaya
C.d: A Swiss man previously convicted of abusing children in Fribourg (1980) and Valais (1991) returned to Thailand in 1996 and, mainly in 2002–2013, abused more than 80 boys in Pattaya, where he ran a bar with a hotel room frequented by Europeans, and in Nong Hoi in the north; he also forced boys to perform acts with European clients. Charged in Fribourg with human trafficking, encouraging prostitution, sexual acts with children and abuse material, he was sentenced by a Swiss court on 1 March 2018 to 16 years.
C.cite: Al Jazeera, 10 Mar 2017; swissinfo.ch, 1 Mar 2018

C.n: Mark Frost — 13 life terms for abuse of boys in Thailand and the UK (2017)
C.vn: at least nine children in Thailand; 45 offences in total
C.who: Mark Frost (also known as Andrew Tracey), former teacher and scout leader
C.d: Frost, who had held positions of trust in UK schools and scouting and first admitted an offence in 1992, abused boys from poor families in Thailand in 2011–2013, including streaming abuse by webcam to another European man. In February 2017 he was sentenced to 13 terms of life imprisonment after pleading guilty to 45 offences against boys in the UK and Thailand. The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse cited the case as one of only about eight successful UK prosecutions since 1997 for offences committed abroad. Eight Thai boys secured civil compensation in 2018.
C.cite: Leigh Day, 20 Nov 2018; IICSA 'Protection of Children Outside the UK' report, Jan 2020; Al Jazeera, 10 Mar 2017

C.n: Patong, Phuket — foreign bar owner sentenced to 1,073 years after raid freed six minors (2024)
C.who: Illegal bar on Bangla Road
C.cover: Five senior Patong police officers were transferred after the raid; the foreign owner initially fled to a neighbouring country.
C.d: A 2023 raid on an illegal bar on Bangla Road, Patong, rescued six victims of child sexual exploitation under 18. On 19 July 2024 the Phuket Provincial Court sentenced seven defendants, Thai and foreign; the prime defendant, a foreign owner, received a total of 1,073 years. Five senior Patong police were transferred after the raid. The 2025 US TIP report says children from Thailand, Burma, Cambodia and Laos are increasingly sex-trafficked in brothels, bars, karaoke lounges and hotels.
C.cite: The Phuket Express, 19 Jul 2024; US TIP 2025 — Thailand

C.n: David Timothy Deakin — life sentence, Angeles City court (2020)
C.vn: two girls rescued at arrest
C.who: David Timothy Deakin (US national)
C.d: Acting on an FBI referral, the Philippine National Bureau of Investigation arrested US national David Timothy Deakin in Mabalacat, Pampanga, in 2017, rescuing two girls and seizing hard drives of abuse material; IJM said he abused Filipino children, recorded it and sold it online to foreign customers. In May 2020 the Angeles City Regional Trial Court Branch 58 convicted him of large-scale human trafficking and sentenced him to life imprisonment, in the country's first conviction delivered by videoconference. The 2025 US TIP report names Angeles City among tourist destinations with high demand for commercial sex.
C.cite: Philstar, 28 May 2020; US TIP 2025 — Philippines

C.n: Philippines — foreign offenders and child sex trafficking in tourist towns (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Foreign offenders; family members; brothel and bar operators
C.cover: Corruption and official complicity remained significant concerns.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says sex trafficking frequently occurs in tourist destinations such as Boracay, Angeles City, Olongapo, Puerto Galera and Surigao. Many foreign offenders are convicted or charged sex offenders at home, most commonly from Australia, Japan, New Zealand, the UK and the US, with more reports from Canada, Morocco, Iraq and Denmark. Courts convicted 143 traffickers, 120 for sex trafficking.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Philippines

C.n: Indonesia — child sexual exploitation in the Riau Islands and 'contract marriages' in Puncak (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Foreign offenders; brokers of 'contract marriages'
C.cover: The report says the government tacitly accepted 'contract marriages'; corruption and complicity significantly impeded efforts.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says extraterritorial child sexual exploitation is prevalent in the Riau Islands bordering Singapore, and women and girls are coerced into commercial sex notably in Batam. It also reports that Middle Eastern tourists pay more than $700 for week-long 'contract marriages' in Puncak, Bogor, involving girls as young as nine, a practice the government tacitly accepted. In October 2017 Batam police arrested a Singaporean man accused of molesting three boys (IBTimes, charged).
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Indonesia; IBTimes UK, Oct 2017

C.n: Japan — 'JK business' and compensated dating (police survey 2024; US TIP 2025)
C.who: JK businesses, often with organized-crime ties
C.d: The 'JK business' sells simulated dates and services with high-school girls. A National Police Agency survey at the end of December 2024 counted 91 establishments advertising in this way, 70 per cent in Tokyo. Kanagawa first regulated it in 2011 and Tokyo enacted a dedicated ordinance in 2017. The 2025 US TIP report says JK variants and 'compensated dating', often tied to organized crime, continue to facilitate sex trafficking of Japanese children and of children from China, South Korea, Laos, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam.
C.cite: Wikipedia 'JK business' (citing National Police Agency); US TIP 2025 — Japan

C.n: South Korea — runaway children in commercial sex; police officer convicted (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Entertainment establishments, escort services, chat-room operators
C.cover: NGOs previously reported some local police sexually exploited children; one officer was convicted (bribery, secrecy violations) and another acquitted.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit South Korean women and children, including runaways, in bars, nightclubs and internet-advertised escort services, and chat-room operators coerce children with compromising images into producing sexual material. A court convicted a local police officer in a 2022 case involving alleged complicity in trafficking-related crimes and sentenced him to five years; another officer was acquitted.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — South Korea

C.n: Mongolia — girls sex-trafficked in Ulaanbaatar hotels and karaoke bars (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers in hotels, massage parlours, karaoke clubs
C.cover: The report says exploitation is sometimes facilitated by lack of police enforcement; some families are complicit.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says women and girls are sex-trafficked in Mongolian hotels, massage parlours, illegal brothels, bars and karaoke clubs, mostly in Ulaanbaatar, provincial centres and border areas, sometimes facilitated by a lack of police enforcement; traffickers use online platforms to groom and blackmail children; and children taken abroad for competitions have instead been put to work, e.g. as horse jockeys.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Mongolia

C.n: Sri Lanka — child sex tourism in coastal areas (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Foreign and local offenders
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers reportedly exploit boys and girls in child sex trafficking, including in coastal areas, for foreign offenders, and recommends investigating complicit establishments. The government convicted six traffickers and identified seven child victims in the year.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Sri Lanka

C.n: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan — girls lured to cities; children in institutions (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers recruiting via social media
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers lure girls and women from rural Kazakhstan and neighbouring Central Asian, East Asian and Eastern European countries with job offers as waitresses, models or nannies in large cities, and exploit Kazakh women and girls in Russia, Uzbekistan, the Middle East, Europe, East Asia and the US. In Uzbekistan, children in institutions are vulnerable to sex trafficking.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Kazakhstan; Uzbekistan

C.n: Medellín — US federal prosecutions of travelling offenders (10 convictions by May 2026)
C.vn: Count of US sentences reported by Medellín mayor's office and BluRadio; individual cases cover at least five victims (Poceiro) and a 14-year-old (Arellano Sandoval)
C.who: US-national travelling offenders; HSI Colombia; Alcaldía de Medellín
C.d: BluRadio reported on 21 May 2026 that US courts, working with Colombian authorities and the Medellín mayor's office, had handed down a tenth sentence in an offensive against foreigners exploiting children in Medellín: Ramón Arellano Sandoval, 65, sentenced in Miami to 30 years for attempted sexual exploitation of a 14-year-old Medellín girl, who had entered the city 48 times in two years. On 22 January 2026 Manuel Poceiro, 69, of Miami, was sentenced to life for travelling to Colombia to exploit minors, after HSI found material involving at least five minors. In March 2024 US national Timothy Alan Livingston was found in a Medellín hotel with two minors (aged between 12 and 16, per police sources); a Colombian judge issued an arrest warrant and Interpol a blue notice (charged, at large at the time).
C.cite: BluRadio, 21 May 2026; US Attorney's Office SDFL, 22 Jan 2026; El Tiempo, 9 Apr 2024; La FM, Apr 2024

C.n: Cartagena — 'La Madame' network exploiting girls for tourists (plea 2018)
C.who: Liliana del Carmen Campos Puello ('La Madame')
C.cover: At hearings she threatened to reveal the names of politicians and powerful men she said were clients (her claim, unverified).
C.d: Liliana del Carmen Campos Puello ran a sex network from a Bocagrande apartment in Cartagena, supplying young women and minors to parties on yachts, in hotels and at beaches and sending women to Panama, Mexico, Miami and the Bahamas; prosecutors seized 15 ledgers of clients and payments, and a WhatsApp group listed 200 women. In 2018 she accepted charges of human trafficking and conspiracy in a plea deal and was sentenced to eight years and one month; she was released on parole in 2023. US ICE supported the investigation.
C.cite: La FM, 2018; El Comercio (Peru), 6 Aug 2018; Noticias RCN, 2023

C.n: Colombia — Tren de Aragua sex trafficking of Venezuelan girls; webcam industry (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Tren de Aragua; ELN; webcam studios
C.cover: Two complicit officials received plea-deal sentences of 7.5 years, below the statutory minimum.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says Tren de Aragua and the ELN run sex-trafficking networks in Villa del Rosario, Norte de Santander, and Tren de Aragua uses Cúcuta's transport hub to move victims to Argentina, Ecuador and Peru and operates in Bogotá, Cali, Medellín and Pereira. Traffickers recruit women and girls, mostly Colombians and displaced Venezuelans, into 'webcam modelling', an industry likely worth over $1.2 billion a year. Sex trafficking of girls is prevalent in tourist areas and extractive zones.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Colombia

C.n: Sosúa — 29 trafficking victims including 20 minors freed in US–Dominican sting (2015)
C.vn: including 20 minors aged 14–17
C.who: Local pimping ring in a tourist town
C.d: In April 2015 Dominican authorities, with HSI Santo Domingo and two private US organisations, lured alleged traffickers to a staged 'sex party' in the tourist town of Sosúa, freeing 29 victims including 20 minors aged 14–17 and arresting seven Dominican nationals (two women, five men), who faced up to 15 years. The 2025 US TIP report says teenage girls are frequently exploited on streets, in parks and on beaches, and NGOs link rising child victim numbers to weak regulation of tourism.
C.cite: Latin Times, Apr 2015 (citing El Periódico, US Embassy); US TIP 2025 — Dominican Republic

C.n: La Pampa, Madre de Dios — Operación Mercurio 2019 and sex trafficking in mining camps
C.vn: number of minors rescued in Mercurio 2019 not stated in sources opened
C.who: Bar/brothel networks serving illegal gold-mining camps
C.d: On 19–20 February 2019 more than 1,500 military and police began Operación Mercurio against illegal gold mining in La Pampa, in the Tambopata reserve buffer zone, under a state of emergency. Peru's Women's Minister said the worst crimes, including child sexual exploitation and child labour, had been committed there, and her ministry took in minors and women rescued from trafficking. Reporting in 2022 said police were still dismantling networks recruiting women to La Pampa bars; a 16-year-old girl previously rescued from a La Pampa trafficking band was found murdered at km 108 in April 2021.
C.cite: Andina, 20 Feb 2019; Diálogo Américas, 2019; Actualidad Ambiental, 15 Feb 2022; US TIP 2025 — Peru

C.n: Peru — foreign tourists exploit children in Cusco, Lima and the Amazon (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Criminal groups transporting tourists on the Amazon
C.cover: Authorities charged two police officers for crimes against trafficking victims; corruption remained a significant concern.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says tourists from the US and Europe exploit children in Cusco, Lima and the Peruvian Amazon, and in Loreto criminal groups take foreign tourists by boat to remote venues on the Amazon River where women and children are exploited. Peruvian, Venezuelan and Bolivian women and girls are lured to mining and logging camps. Courts convicted 59 traffickers in 2024.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Peru

C.n: Brazil — Federal Highway Police 'Projeto Mapear' of child sexual exploitation points on highways
C.vn: Mapear 2021–22: 9,700+ points surveyed, 640 critical; 2023 operations rescued 138 minors, 14 being sexually exploited
C.who: Truck stops, bars, motels along federal highways
C.d: Brazil's Federal Highway Police (PRF) and Childhood Brasil have mapped roadside sites vulnerable to child sexual exploitation for about 19 years. The 2021–2022 survey, released 31 May 2023, assessed more than 9,700 points, rating 640 critical and about 1,800 high-risk; the worst conditions were on BR-116 (12 critical points), BR-153, BR-101, BR-163, BR-232 and BR-040. An earlier edition found 69% of victims female and 22% transgender, and 38% from elsewhere, possibly trafficked. The 2025 US TIP report says child sex trafficking is common along BR-386, BR-116 and BR-255.
C.cite: SBT News, 1 Jun 2023; Brasil 61 (PRF/Childhood Brasil); US TIP 2025 — Brazil

C.n: Brazil — child sex tourism in northeastern coastal cities (Fortaleza, Natal, Recife, Salvador)
C.who: Taxi drivers, hotel and bar staff facilitating foreign offenders
C.cover: US TIP 2025: no investigations of complicit officials reported; a 2016 child sex-trafficking case involving an elected official in Paraná unresolved.
C.d: In 2006 Brazil's Federal Police described sex tourism as most frequent in Fortaleza, Recife, Salvador and Natal, and ran periodic raids, e.g. on a Ponta Negra (Natal) nightclub with 110 foreigners (no children found that night). The 2025 US TIP report says taxi drivers and hotel, bar and nightclub staff in coastal tourist destinations facilitate child sex trafficking, and cites a study suggesting up to 16 per cent of girls aged 14–17 in one northeastern metropolitan area were likely victims of commercial sexual exploitation.
C.cite: Agência Brasil, 4 Apr 2006; US TIP 2025 — Brazil

C.n: Bolivia — foreign offenders in Indigenous communities near Rurrenabaque (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Foreign offenders; parents; online abuse-material producers
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says foreign offenders exploited children in rural Indigenous communities in northern La Paz department, in and around Rurrenabaque and Santa Cruz, and in tourist areas of La Paz and Beni; production of abuse material for sale online is rising in Cochabamba, El Alto and Santa Cruz; and Bolivian women and girls are exploited in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Panama and Peru. Tren de Aragua is reported to be involved in trafficking in Bolivia.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Bolivia

C.n: Paraguay — 47,000 children in criadazgo domestic servitude (US TIP 2025)
C.vn: estimate of children in criadazgo
C.who: Families taking in children as unpaid domestic workers
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says criadazgo — compelling children to work as domestic workers — is a common form of trafficking in Paraguay; an estimated 47,000 children are in criadazgo, mostly girls (boys are 30 per cent), and many are highly vulnerable to sex and labour trafficking. Colombia's report describes the same practice.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Paraguay

C.n: Haiti — restavek child domestic servitude and gang exploitation of children (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Host families (restavek); armed gangs
C.cover: Observers report police and immigration officials complicit at the Haiti–Dominican Republic border.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says a large share of Haiti's trafficking cases involve children in restavek domestic servitude, often physically abused and unpaid, and that displacement from Port-au-Prince increased children's risk of sexual exploitation in the restavek system. Gangs exploit women and girls in sex trafficking; an international organization reported close to 50 per cent of gang members are children, with a 70 per cent rise in child recruitment in 2024.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Haiti

C.n: Jamaica — child sex trafficking in resort towns; 6.3% of 12–17-year-olds (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Family members, 'dons', foreign and local buyers
C.cover: Endemic corruption and official complicity, including within law enforcement, remained significant concerns.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report cites a 2023 prevalence study estimating 6.3 per cent of Jamaican children aged 12–17 had experienced conditions indicative of trafficking. Children are subjected to sex trafficking in resort areas frequented by tourists, sometimes with parental involvement, and men pay girls or their families for sex in some communities.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Jamaica

C.n: Costa Rica — child sex trafficking on Pacific coast and borders (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers in coastal tourist zones
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers subject Costa Rican women and children to sex trafficking, especially in Pacific coastal zones and near the northern and southern borders, where social tolerance increases children's vulnerability; girls from Nicaragua, Panama, the Dominican Republic and Venezuela are also identified as victims.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Costa Rica

C.n: Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala — gangs exploit girls; North American offenders (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Gangs and criminal organizations; foreign offenders
C.d: The 2025 US TIP reports say criminal organizations including gangs exploit girls in sex trafficking in urban Honduras and Guatemala, and that men from Canada and the US exploit Honduran children. In El Salvador, foreign tourists sexually exploit children and the rapid growth of tourism has created new risks; an estimated 140,000–200,000 Salvadoran children have a parent abroad or detained. Guatemalan children are exploited in Mexico and the US and in live-streamed abuse.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Honduras; El Salvador; Guatemala

C.n: Europol: at least 10,000 unaccompanied migrant children missing in Europe (2016)
C.vn: Europol called it likely conservative; 5,000 missing in Italy and 1,000 in Sweden
C.who: Europol; organized crime exploiting the migrant flow
C.d: On 31 January 2016 Europol's chief of staff Brian Donald told The Observer that at least 10,000 unaccompanied children had disappeared after arriving in Europe, 5,000 of them in Italy and 1,000 in Sweden, and that Europol had evidence some had been sexually exploited. He said an entire criminal infrastructure had developed over 18 months around exploiting the migrant flow, with many arrests in Germany and Hungary. Save the Children estimated 26,000 unaccompanied children arrived in 2015.
C.cite: The Observer via Christian Science Monitor, 1 Feb 2016

C.n: Romania–UK 'loverboy' network dismantled — 21 arrested (Eurojust, 2020)
C.who: Romanian organized criminal group using the 'loverboy' method
C.d: On 9 September 2020 a Romanian–UK Joint Investigation Team supported by Eurojust arrested 21 members of a hierarchical group active since 2009 that seduced vulnerable Romanian girls with false promises of relationships, exploited minors in prostitution in Romania until they turned 18, and then moved them to the UK, Ireland and Germany. Thirty-two house searches were carried out (23 in Romania, 9 in the UK). Eurojust said Romania and the UK had cooperated in 76 trafficking investigations in four years.
C.cite: Eurojust press release, 18 Sep 2020

C.n: Galați/Brăila — 'loverboy' ring exploiting minors in Western Europe (2021)
C.who: Four suspects detained by DIICOT/BCCO
C.d: In February 2021 Romanian organised-crime police and DIICOT prosecutors searched eight addresses in Galați and Brăila and detained four suspects for human trafficking, trafficking of minors and pimping. Investigators said that from August 2013 the group recruited girls and young women by the 'loverboy' method, hid minors in intermediate lodgings until they turned 18, then exploited them in Western Europe, earning about €350,000; nine victims, minor and adult, had been identified.
C.cite: Știri pe Surse (via News.ro), 10 Feb 2021

C.n: Romania — girls in state institutions at risk; victims sent across Europe (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers; staff of some government-run institutions
C.cover: Alleged complicity, misconduct and negligence by government employees in cases involving children in government-run homes remained a concern.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says most identified victims are women and girls exploited in Romania and in Austria, France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK; children in government-run institutions, particularly girls in homes for persons with disabilities, are at risk of sex trafficking; and Roma children as young as 11 are 'sold' into marriage. Courts convicted 161 traffickers (143 for sex trafficking) and 600 victims were identified in 2024.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Romania

C.n: Bulgaria — girls trafficked to Western Europe; exploitation in state institutions (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers; Roma forced marriages to third-country nationals
C.cover: Corruption in law enforcement and the judiciary and impunity for complicit officials were pervasive; 34 convicted traffickers received suspended sentences.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Bulgarian women and girls in sex trafficking throughout Western Europe and in Sofia, resort areas and border towns, and cites a UN special rapporteur finding that child sexual exploitation, including potential sex trafficking, was prevalent among children in government-run institutions. Courts convicted 31 traffickers; only eight received custodial sentences.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Bulgaria

C.n: Moldova — children recruited online; institution leavers at risk (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers using social media and fake job ads
C.cover: A former police officer was convicted of labour trafficking (20 years); corruption and complicity remained significant concerns.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers increasingly use social media and video chat to recruit children through fake job ads and exploit them in commercial sex, use abuse material as a grooming method, and target children in or leaving state institutions. Courts convicted 33 traffickers (22 for sex trafficking) in 2024.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Moldova

C.n: Ukraine — wartime risk to evacuated institutional children; officials allegedly complicit (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Criminal networks; some institution officials
C.cover: Officials of several state-run residential institutions were allegedly complicit or negligent in trafficking of children in their care; no complicit officials convicted for the eighth year running.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says child sex trafficking in Ukraine is underreported and criminals are trying to build online networks to exploit Ukrainian children internationally; children evacuated from at least 195 facilities, including those with disabilities, are at high risk; and Ukrainian refugee women and children are vulnerable in Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria and the UK. Ukraine convicted 24 traffickers in 2024, only six with prison terms.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Ukraine; Germany; France

C.n: Albania — children exploited in tourist season; first trafficking convictions since 2021 (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Traffickers; families
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Albanian women and children in sex trafficking and forced labour, especially in tourist season; Roma and Balkan-Egyptian children are forced to beg; and Albanian migrants in Western Europe, particularly the UK, are vulnerable to forced criminality. Courts convicted two sex traffickers and two labour traffickers, the first convictions since 2021. In the UK, Albanians were the second most common nationality referred as potential victims in 2024 (2,492), 95 per cent as adults.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Albania; Home Office NRM statistics 2024

C.n: UK — 5,999 child potential victims referred to the National Referral Mechanism (2024)
C.vn: child referrals in 2024 (31% of 19,125); 416 Vietnamese children; 1,845 county-lines referrals
C.who: Home Office (NRM)
C.d: Home Office statistics show 19,125 potential victims of modern slavery referred in 2024, 31 per cent (5,999) children; 78 per cent of child referrals were boys and criminal exploitation was the most common type (48 per cent). UK nationals were 23 per cent of all referrals, three-quarters of them children; Vietnamese nationals were 11 per cent, 416 of them children. In 2017 the Times reported more than 150 Vietnamese minors had gone missing from UK care since 2015.
C.cite: Home Office, Modern Slavery NRM and DtN statistics, end of year summary 2024; Thomson Reuters Foundation via VnExpress, 13 Oct 2017

C.n: France — 10,000–15,000 French teenagers in child sex trafficking (NGO estimate, US TIP 2025)
C.vn: NGO estimate 10,000–15,000 French teenage victims; 3,000–4,000 unaccompanied Comorian children on Mayotte
C.who: Small networks of young French men using romance schemes
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report cites NGO estimates that 10,000 to 15,000 French teenagers are victims of child sex trafficking, says authorities estimate more than half of all trafficking victims in France are French girls and young women exploited by small 'romance' networks, and that traffickers recruit girls in government-funded shelters. Criminal networks force children, mostly from Romania and North Africa, to commit crimes.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — France

C.n: Germany, Spain, Italy, Greece — romance-method pimps, Nigerian networks, unaccompanied children (US TIP 2025)
C.who: 'Loverboy' traffickers; Nigerian cult-linked groups; Eastern European recruiters
C.d: The 2025 US TIP reports say young male traffickers in Germany and Spain coerce girls into sex trafficking through sham romantic relationships; highly organized groups sometimes linked to Nigerian cult organizations exploit Nigerian women and girls in Germany and Italy, in Italy through debt and 'voodoo' rituals; Eastern European girls are recruited online for child sex trafficking in Italy; and in Greece unaccompanied children are vulnerable to sex trafficking and Roma children from Albania, Bulgaria and Romania are forced to beg.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Germany; Spain; Italy; Greece

C.n: Lebanon — Chez Maurice and Silver-B: about 75 Syrian women freed from sex-trafficking ring (2016)
C.vn: about 75 Syrian women freed in March 2016; a 17-year-old Syrian girl found at the same premises in 2011
C.who: Chez Maurice and Silver-B brothels
C.cover: Chez Maurice was raided in late 2011 when a 17-year-old Syrian girl was found trapped there, closed for about three months and reopened. A survivor told Legal Agenda a trafficker claimed he had 'bought the state'.
C.d: In March 2016 Lebanese security forces freed as many as 75 Syrian women from two brothels, Chez Maurice and Silver-B, in the Maameltein red-light district of Jounieh, and arrested and indicted over a dozen people on sex-trafficking charges. HRW said Syrian refugee women were at particular risk and that the same premises had been raided in 2011, when a 17-year-old Syrian girl was found, and later reopened. Lebanon's police identified 87 trafficking victims in 2016, mainly these survivors.
C.cite: Human Rights Watch, 29 Jul 2016; Al Jazeera, 11 Feb 2020

C.n: Jordan and Türkiye — Syrian refugee girls in forced marriages and sex trafficking (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Families and brokers arranging unofficial marriages
C.cover: Türkiye: no investigations of complicit officials reported, though corruption and complicity remained significant concerns.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says Syrian girls in Türkiye — which hosted about 2.9 million displaced Syrians — are forced into marriages in unofficial religious ceremonies, particularly in poor rural regions, and then subjected to domestic servitude and sex trafficking. In Jordan, Syrian refugee women and girls have been sold into forced marriages, and in 2022 authorities investigated a mother for allegedly exploiting her two daughters with foreign tourists.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Türkiye; Jordan

C.n: Iraq — officials allegedly coerce ISIS-affiliated families, including children, into sex (US TIP 2025)
C.who: Security and military officials (alleged, per an international organization); criminal gangs
C.cover: An international organization reported in 2024 that officials coerce family members of detained children into sex acts in exchange for security clearances or civil documents; the government reported no action on official complicity.
C.d: The 2025 US TIP report says women and girls in IDP camps whose relatives have alleged ISIS ties may face sexual exploitation and sex trafficking by security and military officials, and that some officials allegedly exploit such families, including children, in exchange for documents. Criminal gangs reportedly exploit Syrian women and girls at pilgrimage sites, and Yezidi survivors remain at risk of re-trafficking.
C.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Iraq

C.n: US Angel Watch Center — 10,000+ notifications to foreign countries on travelling sex offenders
C.who: US Homeland Security Investigations; CBP; US Marshals Service
C.d: Under International Megan's Law (signed 2016), the Angel Watch Center notifies foreign governments when US registered child sex offenders plan to travel. DHS says that since 2016 it has made more than 10,000 notifications to foreign countries and notified the State Department of more than 3,500 passports carrying a sex-offender endorsement. HSI child-exploitation arrests rose to 3,771 in 2019 (ABC7, at the centre's ribbon-cutting).
C.cite: DHS/HSI 'Angel Watch Center' page; WJLA/ABC7, 14 Nov 2019; Public Law 114-119

C.n: UK — IICSA finds gaps let known offenders abuse children abroad (2020)
C.who: UK Home Office, police, courts
C.cover: IICSA found travel restrictions were rarely used: 11 of 5,551 Sexual Harm Prevention Orders in 2017/18 and six Sexual Risk Orders in force in March 2019.
C.d: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse report on the protection of children outside the UK (January 2020) found that only 11 of the 5,551 Sexual Harm Prevention Orders made in 2017/18 included foreign-travel restrictions, that 361 UK nationals sought consular help after arrest abroad for child sex offences in 2013–2017, and that there appear to have been only about eight successful UK prosecutions since 1997 for offences committed abroad, including Keith Morris (18.5 years, Kenya) and Mark Frost (Thailand).
C.cite: IICSA, 'The Protection of Children Outside the United Kingdom', January 2020

C.n: ECPAT 'Offenders on the Move' — Global Study on Sexual Exploitation of Children in Travel and Tourism (2016)
C.who: ECPAT International and partners (High-Level Task Force chaired by Najat Maalla M'jid)
C.d: Published 12 May 2016 after two years' work, the study found sexual exploitation of children in travel and tourism had grown despite 20 years of effort, as international arrivals rose from 527 million to 1.135 billion a year. It found there is no typical offender: most are domestic or regional travellers and 'situational' offenders rather than Western paedophiles; the internet has opened new pathways; and conviction rates are alarmingly low. It identified the US and Canada as source countries for offenders and Europe as a source, with exploitation rising in Central and Eastern Europe.
C.cite: ECPAT International, Global Study on SECTT, 12 May 2016

C.n: Fr Nicolás Aguilar Rivera — Puebla diocese priest in Los Angeles
C.vn: 26 grade-school children per a 1988 police report
C.who: Archdiocese of Los Angeles; Diocese of Tehuacán (Mexico)
C.cover: Plaintiffs' attorneys produced a 1988 letter from the Bishop of Tehuacán saying he had warned Cardinal Mahony in 1987 about the priest; the archdiocese denied receiving the warning. The priest fled to Mexico after being relieved of duties and was never arrested.
C.d: A visiting Mexican priest was assigned to two Los Angeles parishes in 1987. A 1988 police report says he abused 26 grade-school children between March 1987 and January 1988, many recruited as altar servers. A parent reported abuse to a pastor on 8 January 1988; he was removed the next day, charged with 19 felony counts of lewd acts on a child, but fled to Mexico before arrest. As of 2004 the case remained open.
C.cite: Associated Press, 'Attorneys: Mahony ignored warnings from Mexican bishop', 30 April 2004 (via BishopAccountability.org)

C.n: Fr Joseph Jeyapaul — Indian priest extradited to Minnesota
C.who: Diocese of Crookston, Minnesota; diocese in India
C.cover: The Vatican recommended his removal from the priesthood, but the Indian bishop instead imposed a year in a monastery through a canonical trial, and he continued as a priest in India.
C.d: An Indian priest serving in the Diocese of Crookston in 2004–2005 was removed from ministry in September 2005 and returned to India. He was charged in 2006 with raping a girl from age 14; extradition took about five years after an Interpol alert, with arrest in Erode, India in 2012 and return to Minnesota in November 2014. In 2015 he pleaded guilty to criminal sexual misconduct involving a teenage girl and was sentenced to a year and a day (time served); the rape charges were dismissed under the plea deal and he faced deportation to India.
C.cite: MPR News, 17 Nov 2014; Star Tribune, 15 June 2015

C.n: Fr Johannes Rivoire — Oblate in Nunavut, never extradited from France
C.place: Arviat, Rankin Inlet, Naujaat and Whale Cove, Nunavut
C.vn: review found on the balance of evidence that he assaulted six children, plus evidence of another victim c.1968–70
C.who: Oblates of Mary Immaculate (OMI Lacombe Canada; Oblates of France)
C.cover: He left for France in January 1993; a Canadian arrest warrant followed in 1998 and charges were later stayed. A 2022 warrant led to an extradition request that French authorities denied. The 2024 Denis review found the RCMP never contacted the Oblates when charges were laid. In February 2024 the Vatican ruled against his dismissal. He died in France in 2024 without trial.
C.d: French Oblate Johannes Rivoire worked in the Canadian North from 1959 to 1993. He faced at least three sexual-abuse charges (1998 warrant) concerning Inuit children in Arviat, Rankin Inlet and Naujaat, and a 2022 warrant for indecent assault on a girl in Arviat and Whale Cove between 1974 and 1979. A March 2024 review by retired Quebec justice André Denis, commissioned by the Oblates, concluded on the preponderance of evidence that he assaulted six children. Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami called his death without trial in April 2024 'a systemic failure of nation states and religious institutions'.
C.cite: Canadian Press via Global News, 19 March 2024; Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami statement, 12 April 2024

C.n: Colombia — Constitutional Court orders Medellín archdiocese to release priests' files
C.who: Archdiocese of Medellín; Salesian Inspectorate of San Luis Beltrán, Medellín
C.cover: Both the archdiocese and the Salesian province refused journalist Juan Pablo Barrientos's 2019 request for the records of 43 priests, calling them private; the archdiocese appealed the first-instance ruling against it.
C.d: In May 2019 journalist Juan Pablo Barrientos, author of 'Dejad que los niños vengan a mí', asked the Archdiocese of Medellín and the Salesians for the records of 43 priests, including complaints against them. After both refused, he filed tutela actions. On 3 March 2020 the Constitutional Court ruled that the information was semi-private and that the right to information prevailed, ordering the archdiocese to hand it over. In 2022 the Court agreed to review a further petition covering 915 priests who served in Medellín.
C.cite: El Espectador, 3 March 2020; Infobae, 2 Feb 2022

C.n: Ecuador — 103 complaints of sexual violence against clergy (Ecuavisa)
C.vn: 103 complaints; the outlet calls it an undercount
C.who: Catholic clergy in Ecuador
C.cover: Victims' families said the church hierarchy refused to share information or file complaints with prosecutors itself, contrary to a National Assembly commission report on sexual violence against children in education.
C.d: A months-long investigation by Ecuavisa's Visión 360 counted 103 complaints of sexual abuse involving Ecuadorian clergy, with cases in Guayas, Pichincha, Azuay and Los Ríos, including those of Fr César Cordero and Fr Luis Intriago. A survivors' association demanded that such crimes be made imprescriptible, as approved in a referendum.
C.cite: El Oriente (Ecuador), reporting Ecuavisa Visión 360

C.n: Paraguay — Fr Carlos Urrutigoity and the removal of Bishop Livieres
C.who: Diocese of Ciudad del Este
C.cover: After accusations in the US (a 2002 complaint over students at St Gregory's Academy in the Diocese of Scranton), he moved with his group to Ciudad del Este, where Bishop Rogelio Livieres made him vicar general in 2014. Pope Francis removed Livieres in 2014; Urrutigoity left in June 2015. La Nación reported at least five Argentine priests accused of abuse or crimes against humanity had sheltered in Paraguay.
C.d: Argentine priest Carlos Urrutigoity was accused in 2002 in the US of sleeping with boarding-school students, giving them alcohol and sexually abusing a recently graduated seminarian. He then moved to the Diocese of Ciudad del Este, Paraguay, and became its second-in-command in 2014. His case reportedly cost Bishop Livieres his post when Pope Francis removed him in 2014. He was moved back to Mendoza, Argentina, in June 2015. He has not been convicted.
C.cite: La Nación (Paraguay), 23 May 2016

C.n: Costa Rica — Fr Mauricio Víquez, convicted after fleeing to Mexico
C.who: Archdiocese of San José; Episcopal Conference of Costa Rica
C.cover: A San José civil court ordered Archbishop José Rafael Quirós, the Episcopal Conference and the church's property entity to pay 65 million colones; the victims' lawyer said the church knew from 2002 and did nothing. Three other complaints were declared time-barred.
C.d: Víquez, a former church spokesman on family issues, fled Costa Rica in 2018 when accusations surfaced, going via Panama to San Nicolás de los Garza, Mexico, where he was caught; he was extradited in 2021. The church expelled him from the clergy in 2019. In March 2022 he was sentenced to 20 years (6 for sexual abuse, 14 for rape) for abusing an 11-year-old boy in his parish in 2002–2003. In August 2022 a civil court ordered the archbishop and two church entities to pay about US$100,000 in damages.
C.cite: El Observador (Costa Rica), 30 March 2022; AP via Voz de América, 24 Aug 2022

C.n: Puerto Rico — Arecibo priests defrocked; island-wide probe
C.vn: six priests expelled; at least 11 more under investigation
C.who: Diocese of Arecibo; at least four Puerto Rican dioceses
C.cover: Prosecutor Yolanda Pitino said the diocese's information was insufficient and it had not answered requests for more; Justice Secretary César Miranda warned he might charge church officials suspected of withholding information.
C.d: In early 2014, after reports in El Nuevo Día, Bishop Daniel Fernández disclosed that since 2011 he had expelled six priests accused of sexual abuse in the Arecibo diocese. Local prosecutors said at least 11 other priests on the island were under investigation, and the Justice Secretary said at least four dioceses were being investigated. U.S. Homeland Security Investigations requested information.
C.cite: Associated Press via Fox News, 2014

C.n: Japan — Bishops' Conference survey: 16 cases
C.who: Catholic Bishops' Conference of Japan (16 dioceses)
C.cover: Eight accused clerics were transferred; some punished clerics kept working or moved to another diocese; five remained priests. Only one denied case was examined by a third-party panel.
C.d: The Catholic Bishops' Conference of Japan began a survey of all 16 dioceses in May 2019 and published it on 7 April 2020. It found 16 cases of sexual abuse of minors from the 1950s to the 2010s, called 'the tip of the iceberg'. Most victims took 10 to 30 years to report, some 50 to 70 years. Of the accused, seven were Japanese priests and eight religious or missionaries, seven of them foreign. Earlier internal surveys (2002, 2012) had found two and five cases.
C.cite: Asahi Shimbun, 16 April 2020; CNA / Catholic World Report, 3 April 2020

C.n: IICSA — Child protection in religious organisations and settings (2021)
C.who: 38 religious organisations in England and Wales, including churches, mosques, synagogues, temples and out-of-school faith settings
C.cover: The Inquiry found victim-blaming, discouraging external reporting and putting reputation above victims; some organisations serving large congregations had no child protection policy at all.
C.d: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse published its report on 2 September 2021 after taking evidence from 38 religious organisations. It found child sexual abuse in most major UK religions and 'shocking failings' in prevention and response. An estimated 250,000 children attend faith-based supplementary or out-of-school settings, which need not register with any state body and have no child-protection oversight. Among cases heard, a mosque Qur'an teacher who abused four children aged about nine was convicted in 2017 and jailed for 13 years. It recommended that every religious organisation have a child protection policy and that the law on full-time education be changed so unregistered schools come under Ofsted.
C.cite: IICSA, 'Child protection in religious organisations and settings' investigation report, 2 September 2021

C.n: Methodist Church (Britain) — Past Cases Review
C.vn: 1,885 cases of sexual, physical, emotional and domestic abuse or neglect since 1950, involving children, young people and adults; not all were child sexual abuse
C.who: Methodist Church in Britain
C.cover: The church said abuse by some Methodists had been ignored or not listened to; it issued an 'unreserved apology'.
C.d: Published on 28 May 2015 after three years of research, the Methodist Church's Past Cases Review found 1,885 cases of sexual, physical, emotional and domestic abuse or neglect going back to 1950. In 26% of cases church ministers or lay employees were identified as the alleged perpetrators. Six police investigations were ongoing. General Secretary Martyn Atkins made an unreserved apology.
C.cite: Methodist Church Past Cases Review, May 2015, as reported by AP (Fox News) and Toronto Star, 28 May 2015

C.n: Bob Jones University — GRACE report
C.vn: 50 people who self-identified as victims of sexual abuse were interviewed; many had suffered child sexual abuse before arriving
C.who: Bob Jones University (independent fundamentalist Christian)
C.cover: Several victims said campus counselors did not report their abuse to legal authorities; counseling blamed victims and treated all 'sexual sin' as equal. The university fired and then rehired GRACE during the investigation.
C.d: Bob Jones University hired GRACE (Godly Response to Abuse in the Christian Environment) in November 2012 to review its handling of sexual abuse. GRACE's roughly 300-page report, released 11 December 2014, found the school responded to abuse claims with ignorance of state reporting law, little trauma training and a culture that blamed victims; some counselors encouraged victims to repent. The review was prompted in part by a board member's handling of a 1997 case in which a minor girl raped by a church deacon in New Hampshire was made to confess before the congregation. The university president apologised.
C.cite: GRACE, Final Report on Bob Jones University, 11 Dec 2014, as reported by RNS (Christian Century) and The American Prospect, Dec 2014

C.n: Royal Commission Case Study 36 — Church of England Boys' Society
C.place: Tasmania, Adelaide, Brisbane and Sydney dioceses
C.who: Church of England Boys' Society (now Anglican Boys' Society / Boys' Ministry Australia); Anglican dioceses of Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide and Tasmania
C.cover: Allegations were not reported to police at all or not in time; a parish priest told one victim to 'let sleeping dogs lie'. The report found Peter Hollingworth, former Archbishop of Brisbane and later Governor-General, made 'a serious error of judgment' in letting an accused priest continue in ministry.
C.d: The Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse reported in February 2017 that the CEBS youth group gave paedophiles easy access to boys from the 1970s to the 1990s, with abuse on camps, sailing and fishing trips and overnight stays at rectories. It found 'networks of sexual perpetrators at CEBS who had knowledge of each other's sexual offending against boys and in some instances facilitated' it; several associated men were later convicted. It found a focus on protecting the reputation of the church, dioceses, CEBS and clergy.
C.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study No. 36, Feb 2017, as reported by Illawarra Mercury (Fairfax), 13 Feb 2017

C.n: Royal Commission Case Study 42 — Anglican Diocese of Newcastle
C.vn: 19 male victims in Fr James Brown's 2011 convictions alone
C.who: Anglican Diocese of Newcastle (Bishops Alfred Holland 1978–92, Roger Herft 1993–2005)
C.cover: Found a 'do nothing' approach under Bishop Holland and a 'weak and ineffectual' response under Bishop Herft; complainants were treated as liars and sometimes threatened with legal action; abusive relationships were misrepresented as consensual; dioceses receiving moved clergy were not warned; diocesan lawyers acted for accused priests. Former dean Graeme Lawrence was defrocked.
C.d: The Royal Commission's report, released on 7 December 2017 after hearings in August and November 2016, found systemic issues let a group of perpetrators operate in the diocese for at least 30 years. Fr Peter Rushton died in 2007 never charged, though the diocese acknowledges he was a child sex offender. Fr James Brown pleaded guilty in 2011 to 27 child sexual abuse charges relating to 19 boys and was jailed for up to 20 years. Bishop Herft resigned as Archbishop of Perth in 2016. Later bishops Brian Farran and Greg Thompson acted against alleged perpetrators and faced backlash.
C.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study No. 42, 7 Dec 2017, as reported by Newcastle Herald and AAP

C.n: Nigeria — Kaduna 'Islamic school' raid frees 300+ boys and men
C.vn: more than 300 boys and men, some as young as five; sexual abuse reported by local media, not confirmed by Reuters
C.who: Imam Ahmad Bun Hambal Centre for Islamic Studies (purported Islamic school / rehabilitation centre)
C.d: On 26 September 2019 Kaduna police raided a building signed as an Islamic studies centre and freed more than 300 boys and men, many chained and with whip scars. Some had been brought from Burkina Faso, Mali and Ghana; families said they were denied access. Seven people claiming to be teachers were arrested. Local media reported captives were tortured, starved and sexually abused. The raid led to further rescues from similar 'torture houses' in northern Nigeria.
C.cite: Reuters via Africanews, 27 Sept 2019

C.n: Thailand — Chiang Dao monks arrested for procuring a boy for an abbot
C.who: Temple in Chiang Dao (Theravada Buddhist)
C.d: On 19 June 2013 Chiang Mai police arrested two young monks, aged 20 and 23, accused of repeatedly taking a 14-year-old boy to a temple abbot for sexual services since February. Police said the two faced up to 15 years in jail; the abbot had not yet been arrested pending a warrant.
C.cite: Chiang Mai CityNews, 20 June 2013, citing AFP

C.n: Brazil — three Arapiraca priests convicted (Penedo diocese)
C.who: Diocese of Penedo
C.cover: According to the victims, Bishop Valério Breda knew what was happening; he suspended the priests two days after the scandal broke. The convicted priests were not jailed pending appeal.
C.d: On 19 December 2011 a juvenile court judge in Arapiraca convicted Monsignor Luiz Marques Barbosa (21 years), Monsignor Raimundo Gomes and Fr Edílson Duarte (16 years 4 months each) of abusing altar boys. The case began with complaints from former altar boys in March 2010 and a secretly filmed video broadcast on SBT television.
C.cite: Bocão News (Agência Estado), 20 Dec 2011

C.n: Mexico — bishops say 152 priests removed in nine years
C.who: Mexican Episcopal Conference (CEM)
C.cover: The CEM president said there was no national count of victims because 'each bishop handles these problems' and no central record exists.
C.d: On 10 February 2019 Archbishop Rogelio Cabrera of Monterrey, president of the Mexican Episcopal Conference, said 152 priests had been removed from ministry in the previous nine years after being found guilty of sexually abusing minors, some of whom were jailed. He said there was no exact figure for victims.
C.cite: ACI Prensa, 10 Feb 2019

C.n: Amish bishop charged for not reporting abuse confession (Lancaster County)
C.who: Old Order Amish church district, Lancaster County
C.cover: Witnesses said the bishop had the matter 'handled internally' to keep it quiet; the church excommunicated the abuser but did not notify police.
C.d: In April 2020 Amish bishop Levi Esh Sr., 63, was arraigned on felony and misdemeanour charges for failing to report a church member's confession to sexually assaulting three girls around 2012–2013. Pennsylvania law requires clergy to report child abuse.
C.cite: Associated Press via WITF, 23 April 2020

C.n: Amish bishop pleads guilty to failure to report (Dauphin County)
C.place: Mifflin Township / Elizabethville, Dauphin County, Pennsylvania
C.vn: two cases
C.who: Amish church district, Dauphin County
C.cover: Told of two abuse cases in 2011, the bishop did not report them and told police he had been told one 'wasn't really that bad'.
C.d: Amish bishop Christ M. Stoltzfus, 70, pleaded guilty in Dauphin County court in September 2017 to failure to report child abuse and received three months' probation. A church member had told him in 2011 about two cases of child sexual abuse by another member; state police began investigating in January 2017 after a confidential tip.
C.cite: PennLive via BishopAccountability.org Abuse Tracker, Sept 2017

C.n: Myanmar — Pathein monastery: four schoolgirls raped
C.place: Saitta Thuka monastery, Yetho village near Pathein, Ayeyarwady
C.who: Saitta Thuka monastery (Theravada Buddhist monastic boarding)
C.cover: The monk disappeared when parents went to police; TIME found police unable or unwilling to say whether a search continued, and described near-blanket immunity for monks, with police deferring to the religious affairs ministry and the Sangha. An ex-monk who reprimanded him was told to move away.
C.d: Four girls aged 10 to 14 staying free at a monastery so they could attend school were repeatedly raped from June 2017 by the monastery's administrator monk, according to the children and families interviewed by Myanmar Now. The abuse came to light in February 2018; police issued orders to arrest him on sight across several regions. TIME reported up to 300,000 children may live in Myanmar monasteries, with few records kept.
C.cite: Myanmar Now, 2018; TIME, 6 Dec 2018

C.n: Romania — former Bishop of Huși jailed for raping a seminary pupil
C.place: Huși, Vaslui County (St John Chrysostom Orthodox Theological Seminary)
C.who: Romanian Orthodox Church, Diocese of Huși; Huși Orthodox Theological Seminary
C.cover: The case surfaced in June 2017 when the bishop himself complained to anti-corruption prosecutors that three priests were blackmailing him with a recording; a former archimandrite was earlier jailed for that blackmail.
C.d: Romania's High Court of Cassation and Justice upheld a Galați Court of Appeal ruling sentencing former Bishop Corneliu Bârlădeanu (Cornel Onilă) to eight years for rape and other sexual assaults, in a case that began with 2017 recordings allegedly showing him with a minor pupil of the Huși seminary. Former archimandrite Sebastian Jitaru received 14 years 2 months for rape and sexual assaults. The diocese and seminary were ordered to pay court costs; the diocese apologised to the victims. Bârlădeanu resigned in August 2017. Media described him as the first senior Romanian Orthodox hierarch to go to prison.
C.cite: Radio Free Europe Romania (Europa Liberă), citing Agerpres, 2025

C.n: Afghanistan — students report sexual abuse in Taliban-run madrasahs
C.place: Western and southwestern Afghanistan (incl. Farah Province)
C.who: Taliban-run madrasah system (6,836 male madrasahs per a Feb 2024 UN report)
C.cover: A 16-year-old said he reported a teacher to the school's qari, who only told the teacher to stop; the teacher admitted it and continued. The schools are run by the de facto Taliban authorities.
C.d: In March 2024 RFE/RL's Radio Azadi published accounts from male students aged 10 to 17 at Taliban-run madrasahs in western and southwestern Afghanistan who said teachers pressured them and classmates into sexual acts and used corporal punishment; some left school. The report cited a February 2024 UN report counting 6,836 Taliban-established madrasahs for boys and a decree seeking 100,000 new madrasah teachers.
C.cite: RFE/RL Radio Azadi, 10 March 2024

C.n: Ferns Report — Diocese of Ferns
C.vn: More than 100 allegations made between 1962 and 2002
C.who: Catholic Diocese of Ferns
C.cover: Bishop Herlihy moved accused priests to other posts or dioceses for a period, then reinstated them; Gardaí failed to record or properly investigate some pre-1988 complaints
C.d: The state Ferns Inquiry, published 25 October 2005, examined more than 100 allegations of child sexual abuse made between 1962 and 2002 against 21 priests of the diocese. Bishop Donal Herlihy moved accused priests temporarily and then reinstated them, and ordained men he knew or should have known posed a risk. Bishop Brendan Comiskey never got a priest to stand aside from ministry. The report found Garda handling of one of eight formal complaints 'wholly inadequate' and some pre-1988 complaints were not recorded.
C.cite: Ferns Inquiry report, 25 October 2005, as reported by RTÉ News

C.n: Murphy Report — Archdiocese of Dublin
C.vn: 320 people complained of abuse 1975–2004; a further 130 complaints after May 2004
C.who: Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin
C.cover: Abuse 'covered up' 1975–2004; bishops generally did not report to Gardaí before 1996; archdiocese took out insurance against abuse litigation from 1987; Gardaí knew of complaints against Fr Tony Walsh in 1990–91 and took no action
C.d: The Commission of Investigation into the Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin reported on 26 November 2009. It examined a representative sample of 46 priests out of 102 within its remit; 320 people complained of child sexual abuse between 1975 and 2004. It found former Archbishops McQuaid, Ryan, McNamara and Connell failed to report what they knew to the Gardaí, and said the archdiocese's move to take out insurance against abuse claims showed it knew abuse was a potential major cost. It also criticised the Gardaí for treating priests as outside their remit; the Garda Commissioner called the report 'difficult and disturbing reading'.
C.cite: The Guardian, 'Irish church and police covered up child sex abuse, says report', 26 November 2009; RTÉ News, 'Litany of abuse in Dublin Archdiocese', 26 November 2009

C.n: Cloyne Report — Diocese of Cloyne
C.who: Catholic Diocese of Cloyne; Bishop John Magee
C.cover: Nine complaints that should have gone to the Gardaí were not reported; none of the 1996–2008 complaints reported to the health service; Vatican's reaction to Irish guidelines described as 'entirely unhelpful'
C.d: The Cloyne Report, published 13 July 2011, examined the diocese's handling of allegations against 19 clerics from 1996 to February 2009, after the Irish church had adopted reporting procedures. Nine complaints that should have been reported to the Gardaí were not, and none were reported to the health authorities. Bishop John Magee was found to have shown little interest in applying the guidelines for 12 years. The report said the Vatican's response to the Irish procedures allowed bishops to ignore them.
C.cite: Commission of Investigation, Report into the Catholic Diocese of Cloyne, July 2011, as summarised by the Irish Times

C.n: Ryan Commission — industrial schools run by religious orders
C.vn: More than 30,000 children were sent to the institutions; redress scheme paid about 12,000 people
C.who: Christian Brothers (most boys' institutions), Sisters of Mercy (most girls' institutions) and other Catholic orders
C.cover: Christian Brothers sued the commission in 2004 to keep members' names out; no real names of perpetrators published; findings not to be used for prosecutions; state Department of Education inspections failed
C.d: The Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse reported on 20 May 2009 after a nine-year investigation of more than 250 church-run institutions that held over 30,000 children from the 1930s to the 1990s. It found sexual abuse 'endemic' in boys' institutions run mainly by the Christian Brothers; the Sisters of Mercy ran most girls' institutions. The 2,600-page report names no perpetrators after a Christian Brothers lawsuit. A parallel state redress scheme paid about 12,000 people an average of €65,000.
C.cite: Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse (Ryan Report), 20 May 2009, as reported by CBS News/AP

C.n: Scoping Inquiry — abuse in religious-run schools
C.vn: 2,395 allegations recorded; report says true number likely higher
C.who: 42 religious orders that ran day and boarding schools
C.d: The state Scoping Inquiry, published 3 September 2024, recorded 2,395 allegations of sexual abuse against 884 alleged abusers at 308 schools run by 42 religious orders, mostly from the 1960s to the 1990s. 590 allegations involving 190 alleged abusers concerned 17 special schools. More than half of the alleged abusers are dead. The government announced a full Commission of Investigation.
C.cite: Report of the Scoping Inquiry into Historical Sexual Abuse in Day and Boarding Schools Run by Religious Orders, 3 September 2024

C.n: Archdiocese of Boston — Spotlight 2002 and Massachusetts AG report 2003
C.vn: At least 789 minors; AG estimated the true number probably exceeds 1,000
C.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston; Cardinal Bernard Law
C.cover: Accused priests reassigned with Cardinal Law's personal involvement; church alerted law enforcement only twice in six decades; bishops sought leniency for priests and withheld information from prosecutors
C.d: After the Boston Globe Spotlight series beginning January 2002, Cardinal Law resigned in December 2002. The Massachusetts Attorney General's report of 23 July 2003 found at least 237 priests and 13 other church workers accused of abusing at least 789 minors over six decades, and 'overwhelming evidence' that Law knew and took part in reassigning abusers. No criminal statute allowed charging church leaders.
C.cite: Office of the Massachusetts Attorney General, 'The Sexual Abuse of Children in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston', 23 July 2003, as reported by the Boston Globe

C.n: Pennsylvania grand jury — six dioceses
C.place: Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, Allentown, Scranton, Greensburg, Erie
C.vn: 'At least 1,000' identified; grand jury believed there were more
C.who: Six Pennsylvania Catholic dioceses
C.cover: Abusers moved and protected, some later promoted; reports brushed aside; most crimes beyond statute of limitations
C.d: A 23-member statewide grand jury report released by Attorney General Josh Shapiro on 14 August 2018 identified 301 'predator priests' and at least 1,000 child victims over about 70 years in six dioceses. The roughly 1,400-page report found bishops 'went to great lengths to keep it secret' and moved abusers. Most crimes were too old to prosecute.
C.cite: 40th Statewide Investigating Grand Jury report, 14 August 2018, as reported by America magazine

C.n: Illinois Attorney General — clergy abuse report
C.who: Six Catholic dioceses of Illinois
C.cover: Before the investigation the dioceses had publicly listed only 103 substantiated abusers
C.d: Attorney General Kwame Raoul's report of 23 May 2023, from an investigation opened in 2018, named 451 Catholic clerics and religious brothers who abused at least 1,997 children in Illinois' six dioceses over decades. Before the inquiry the dioceses had publicly listed 103 substantiated abusers.
C.cite: Illinois Attorney General, Report on Catholic Clergy Child Sex Abuse in Illinois, 23 May 2023

C.n: John Jay College study — US Catholic clergy 1950–2002
C.place: United States (commissioned by US bishops, Washington DC)
C.vn: 10,667 individuals reported abuse to bishops; authors say true number likely higher
C.who: US Conference of Catholic Bishops (commissioned study)
C.cover: Of accused priests whose cases reached police, only one in three was charged; 3% served prison time
C.d: The John Jay College of Criminal Justice study, commissioned by the US bishops and released 27 February 2004, counted 4,392 priests and deacons (about 4% of clergy) accused of abusing 10,667 minors between 1950 and 2002. Reported abuse peaked in the 1970s; one-third of allegations were made only in 2002–03. 149 priests with more than 10 allegations each accounted for 27% of allegations. Costs to the church were put at $472 million at the time.
C.cite: John Jay College, 'The Nature and Scope of Sexual Abuse of Minors by Catholic Priests and Deacons in the United States 1950–2002', 2004, as summarised by America magazine

C.n: Maryland Attorney General — Archdiocese of Baltimore
C.vn: 'Over 600' children; report says true number 'likely far higher'
C.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Baltimore
C.cover: Archdiocese often failed to report to authorities or remove abusers; some accused allowed to retire with support; post-2002 public list omitted known abusers
C.d: The Maryland Attorney General's report, released in redacted form on 5 April 2023, identified 156 priests and others associated with the Archdiocese of Baltimore who abused more than 600 children over 80 years. Attorney General Anthony Brown described 'repeated coverup' by the church. A judge ordered the names and titles of 37 people redacted.
C.cite: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Report on Child Sexual Abuse in the Archdiocese of Baltimore, 5 April 2023, as reported by Fortune/AP

C.n: Missouri Attorney General — four Catholic dioceses
C.who: Archdiocese of St. Louis and dioceses of Kansas City–St. Joseph, Jefferson City, Springfield–Cape Girardeau
C.d: Attorney General Eric Schmitt reported on 13 September 2019 on a review, opened in August 2018, of records of more than 2,000 priests who served in Missouri since 1945. It found 163 credible allegations of abuse or misconduct against minors by diocesan priests and deacons; 83 of the accused had died and the statute of limitations had expired for 46 alleged crimes. Twelve former priests were referred for prosecution.
C.cite: Missouri Attorney General's Office, clergy abuse report, 13 September 2019, as reported by NPR/KPBS

C.n: Michigan Attorney General — clergy abuse investigation
C.vn: 552 victims identified by December 2019; AG expected 'several thousand' by the end
C.who: Catholic dioceses of Michigan
C.d: Attorney General Dana Nessel said on 23 December 2019 that the state investigation had identified 270 priests alleged to have abused 552 victims. Seven priests had been charged in 2019, two of whom had pleaded guilty. Most cases could not be prosecuted because of statutes of limitations.
C.cite: Detroit News, 23 December 2019, reposted by BishopAccountability.org; Michigan AG press releases

C.n: Archdiocese of Agaña — Archbishop Apuron and bankruptcy
C.vn: More than 220 former altar boys, students and Boy Scouts sued
C.who: Archdiocese of Agaña; former Archbishop Anthony Apuron
C.d: A Vatican tribunal of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith found former Archbishop Anthony Apuron guilty of some charges including sexual abuse of minors in March 2018; the appeal was rejected in February 2019. He was barred from office and from living in Guam but not laicised; he denies the allegations. The archdiocese filed for bankruptcy in January 2019 facing more than 200 lawsuits naming 35 clergy, teachers and scoutmasters. Guam lifted the civil statute of limitations in 2016.
C.cite: Catholic News Agency/EWTN News, 8 August 2019; America magazine, 9 November 2018

C.n: Winter Commission — Archdiocese of St. John's
C.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of St. John's; Archbishop Alphonsus Penney
C.cover: Report assigned Archbishop Penney part of the blame for covering up abuse
C.d: Archbishop Alphonsus Penney commissioned former Lieutenant Governor Gordon Winter in May 1989 to inquire into sexual abuse of children by clergy of the archdiocese. The 1990 report assigned Penney part of the blame for covering up abuse, and he resigned after its release.
C.cite: Report of the Archdiocesan Commission of Enquiry into the Sexual Abuse of Children by Members of the Clergy (Winter Report), 1990

C.n: Royal Commission — Catholic Church data, Australia
C.vn: 4,444 people reported abuse at more than 1,000 Catholic institutions (claims 1980–2015)
C.who: Catholic Church in Australia, incl. St John of God Brothers (40.4% of brothers accused)
C.d: Data presented to the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse on 6 February 2017 showed 4,444 people reported abuse to Catholic authorities between 1980 and 2015, at more than 1,000 institutions, naming 1,880 alleged perpetrators. About 7% of priests who served between 1950 and 2010 were alleged perpetrators; 40.4% of St John of God Brothers were accused. Religious brothers (32%) and priests (30%) were the largest groups. The commission referred 309 cases to police.
C.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Case Study 50 data, 6 February 2017, as reported by NPR

C.n: Diocese of Ballarat — Gerald Ridsdale and Royal Commission Case Study 28
C.vn: Convicted of abusing more than 70 children; advocates estimate hundreds
C.who: Catholic Diocese of Ballarat; Bishop Ronald Mulkearns
C.cover: Ridsdale moved through about 13 postings 1962–1991; Mulkearns knew by late 1975; a senior police officer in 1972 offered a detective promotion to stop investigating Monsignor John Day
C.d: Gerald Ridsdale, ordained 1961, was convicted in a series of trials from 1993 of abusing more than 70 children; he died in prison in 2025. He was moved between parishes including Mildura, Swan Hill, Warrnambool, Apollo Bay, Edenhope and Mortlake, then to Sydney. The Royal Commission's Ballarat report of 6 December 2017 found Bishop Mulkearns knew of his offending by late 1975 and still reappointed him, a 'catastrophic' failure. It also found police obstruction of a 1972 investigation of Monsignor John Day.
C.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study 28 (Ballarat), December 2017; The Courier (Ballarat)

C.n: Royal Commission into Abuse in Care — Catholic institutions
C.vn: About 200,000 abused across all state and faith-based care 1950–2019 (not Catholic alone); church data showed 14% of NZ clergy accused 1950–1999
C.who: Catholic Church in Aotearoa New Zealand; St John of God Brothers at Marylands School
C.cover: Church relied on psychiatrists' opinions to transfer abusers to other ministries where they reoffended; commission recommended investigating priests transferred to Papua New Guinea
C.d: The Royal Commission's final report, Whanaketia, published 24 July 2024, found about 200,000 people were abused in state and faith-based care from 1950 to 2019. It found Catholic responses inadequate, noting a 2020 church briefing that 14% of clergy were accused over 1950–1999, and singled out Marylands School in Christchurch for some of the highest levels of sexual abuse. It found abusers were transferred to other ministries and recommended an inquiry into priests sent to Papua New Guinea.
C.cite: Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care, Whanaketia, 24 July 2024, as reported by EWTN/CNA

C.n: IICSA — Roman Catholic Church in England and Wales
C.vn: More than 900 complaints involving over 3,000 instances of abuse, 1970–2015
